Run a single batch of a TURF analysis

Source: R/turf.R
run_batch.Rd

Scores every combination of size products drawn from possible_products (excluding fixed) by marginal reach: the number of respondents it reaches who are not already reached by fixed. This is one step of turf(), exposed for inspection.

Usage

run_batch(df, possible_products, size, fixed = NA, keep_n = 20)

Arguments

df

A data frame or matrix of activations, with one row per respondent and one column per product. Columns named in possible_products or fixed must contain only 0 and 1. Other columns are ignored.

possible_products

A character vector of the products (column names of df) to choose from.

size

The number of products in each combination. A positive integer no greater than the number of products in possible_products but not in fixed.

fixed

A character vector of products already chosen, or NA for none.

keep_n

The number of combinations to keep. A positive integer.

Value

A list with elements:

  • combos: a character matrix with size rows and one column per kept combination, best first.

  • reach: an integer vector of each kept combination's marginal reach.

  • n_combinations: the number of combinations scored.

Details

Combinations are ranked by marginal reach, then marginal frequency (total activations among respondents not reached by fixed), then the order of their products in possible_products. Scoring runs in Rust.

Examples

batch <- run_batch(am, colnames(am), size = 2, keep_n = 3)
batch$combos
#>      [,1]        [,2]        [,3]       
#> [1,] "southwind" "southwind" "southwind"
#> [2,] "coi"       "lemon"     "may"      

# The best products to add to the current leader
run_batch(am, colnames(am), size = 1, fixed = batch$combos[, 1], keep_n = 3)
#> $combos
#>      [,1]    [,2]  [,3]   
#> [1,] "lemon" "may" "green"
#> 
#> $reach
#> [1] 1587 1544 1526
#> 
#> $n_combinations
#> [1] 51
#>
